title: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis - Bird Fancier's Lung

scenario.setting: Respiratory outpatient clinic, Westmead Hospital, Sydney
scenario.presentation: A 62-year-old retired librarian presents with 4 months of progressive dyspnoea, dry cough, and 5kg weight loss. She reports feeling breathless when climbing stairs and has noticed fevers in the evenings. Symptoms improve when she visits her daughter in Melbourne for a week but return upon coming home. She keeps 6 budgerigars in her living room and has done so for the past 18 months.

vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: 91% on room air, 96% on 2L nasal prongs

scenario.past_medical_history: Hypertension (well-controlled on perindopril 5mg daily), osteoarthritis, no previous respiratory disease
scenario.medications: Perindopril 5mg daily (PBS code: 8218H), Paracetamol 1g PRN (PBS code: 1725Y)
scenario.social_history: Never smoker, retired librarian, lives alone in Parramatta unit with 6 budgerigars, no occupational dust exposures, drinks 1 glass wine weekly
scenario.family_history: Mother had rheumatoid arthritis, father died of stroke at age 78

physical_examination.general: Alert, oriented, mild respiratory distress at rest, using accessory muscles, no clubbing or cyanosis
physical_examination.cardiovascular: JVP not elevated, apex beat not displaced, dual heart sounds with no murmurs, no peripheral oedema
physical_examination.respiratory: Bilateral fine end-inspiratory crackles in mid-to-lower zones, no wheeze, reduced chest expansion bilaterally (3cm), resonant percussion throughout
physical_examination.other_findings: No lymphadenopathy, no skin rashes, normal joint examination

initial_tests.chest_xray: Bilateral reticulonodular infiltrates predominantly in upper and mid zones with sparing of costophrenic angles
initial_tests.arterial_blood_gas: pH 7.44, PaO2 68mmHg, PaCO2 32mmHg, HCO3 22mmol/L, SaO2 91% on room air
initial_tests.full_blood_count: WCC 11.2 x10^9/L (neutrophils 7.8, lymphocytes 2.9, eosinophils 0.3), Hb 118g/L, platelets 312 x10^9/L

specialized_tests.hrct_chest: Ground-glass opacification with mosaic attenuation pattern, centrilobular nodules, air trapping on expiratory views, no honeycombing
specialized_tests.pulmonary_function_tests: FEV1 68% predicted, FVC 65% predicted, FEV1/FVC 82%, DLCO 48% predicted, restrictive pattern
specialized_tests.serum_precipitins: Positive IgG antibodies to budgerigar serum, feathers, and droppings (titre 1:128)
specialized_tests.bronchoalveolar_lavage: Lymphocytosis 48% (normal <15%), CD4/CD8 ratio 0.8, no malignant cells, negative cultures

management_plan.immediate: Supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 >92%, advise complete avoidance of bird exposure, relocate budgerigars immediately
management_plan.medications: Prednisolone 40mg daily (PBS code: 2622X) for 4 weeks then taper over 3 months, continue perindopril
management_plan.monitoring: Weekly spirometry initially, repeat HRCT in 3 months, monitor for steroid side effects
management_plan.long_term: Permanent bird avoidance, home environmental assessment, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination, pulmonary rehabilitation referral

scoring_criteria: Identifies temporal relationship between symptoms and bird exposure (2 marks)
Recognises improvement when away from home as key diagnostic clue (2 marks)
Orders appropriate serum precipitin testing for avian antigens (2 marks)
Correctly interprets restrictive pattern on PFTs with reduced DLCO (2 marks)
Identifies lymphocytosis on BAL as supporting diagnosis (1 mark)
Recommends immediate and complete antigen avoidance (3 marks)
Prescribes appropriate corticosteroid dose and duration (2 marks)
Explains prognosis depends on early recognition and antigen avoidance (2 marks)
Arranges appropriate follow-up with serial PFTs and imaging (2 marks)
Discusses home environmental modifications required (2 marks)
Addresses infection prevention with vaccinations (1 mark)

title: Goodpasture Syndrome - Pulmonary-Renal Syndrome

scenario.setting: Emergency Department, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, Sydney
scenario.presentation: A 28-year-old plasterer presents with 2 weeks of progressive haemoptysis, now coughing up approximately 50mL of fresh blood daily. He reports severe fatigue, dyspnoea on minimal exertion, and noticed his urine has been 'tea-coloured' for the past 5 days. He had an upper respiratory tract infection 3 weeks ago. No chest pain, no joint pains, no skin rashes.

vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: 88% on room air, 94% on 6L Hudson mask

scenario.past_medical_history: Previously well, no chronic medical conditions, tonsillectomy age 8
scenario.social_history: Plasterer for 8 years with intermittent hydrocarbon solvent exposure, smokes 15 cigarettes daily for 10 years, drinks 6 standard drinks on weekends, lives with partner
scenario.family_history: No renal disease, no autoimmune conditions

physical_examination.general: Pale, unwell appearance, respiratory distress, no peripheral oedema, no rashes, conjunctival pallor
physical_examination.cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, normal heart sounds, no murmurs, BP elevated, JVP 3cm above sternal angle
physical_examination.respiratory: Bilateral coarse crackles throughout all lung fields, no wheeze, dull percussion bases bilaterally suggesting effusions
physical_examination.renal: Mild bilateral flank tenderness, no palpable kidneys, no suprapubic tenderness
physical_examination.other_findings: No joint swelling, no nasal crusting or saddle deformity, no oral ulcers

initial_tests.renal_function: Creatinine 342 μmol/L (baseline 78), urea 18.2 mmol/L, eGFR 19 mL/min/1.73m²
initial_tests.urinalysis: Blood 3+, protein 3+, RBC casts present, dysmorphic RBCs >80%
initial_tests.chest_xray: Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates with perihilar predominance, small bilateral pleural effusions

specialized_tests.anca: Negative for both PR3 and MPO
specialized_tests.renal_biopsy: Linear IgG deposition along glomerular basement membrane on immunofluorescence, crescentic glomerulonephritis affecting 75% of glomeruli
specialized_tests.bronchoscopy: Fresh blood in all segments, progressive bleeding during procedure, BAL shows haemosiderin-laden macrophages

management_plan.immediate: High-flow oxygen 15L non-rebreather mask, urgent ICU review, blood transfusion 2 units packed RBCs, IV methylprednisolone 1g daily for 3 days
management_plan.definitive_treatment: Urgent plasmapheresis daily for 14 days, cyclophosphamide 2mg/kg/day PO (PBS code: 1797X), continue prednisolone 60mg daily (PBS code: 1950W)
management_plan.supportive: Fluid restriction 1.5L daily, commence haemodialysis via temporary vascular catheter, PPI prophylaxis with pantoprazole 40mg daily (PBS code: 8523L)
management_plan.monitoring: Daily anti-GBM antibody levels during plasmapheresis, renal function twice daily, daily FBC for cyclophosphamide monitoring, chest X-ray daily while haemoptysis present

scoring_criteria: Recognises pulmonary-renal syndrome presentation (2 marks)
Orders anti-GBM antibodies as primary diagnostic test (3 marks)
Identifies need for urgent renal biopsy for confirmation (2 marks)
Initiates high-dose corticosteroids immediately (2 marks)
Arranges urgent plasmapheresis within 24 hours (3 marks)
Prescribes cyclophosphamide with appropriate dosing (2 marks)
Recognises smoking and hydrocarbon exposure as risk factors (1 mark)
Monitors for treatment complications including infections (2 marks)
Arranges ICU admission for potential respiratory failure (2 marks)
Discusses prognosis related to crescent percentage on biopsy (2 marks)
Coordinates multidisciplinary care with nephrology and respiratory (1 mark)

title: Wegener's Granulomatosis (GPA) - Upper and Lower Respiratory Disease

scenario.setting: Respiratory clinic, John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle
scenario.presentation: A 45-year-old teacher presents with 3 months of recurrent sinusitis, epistaxis, and progressive dyspnoea. She has been treated with 4 courses of antibiotics without improvement. She reports bloody nasal discharge, hearing loss in her right ear, and has developed painful red eyes. Over the past 2 weeks, she has noticed haemoptysis and night sweats with 4kg weight loss.
scenario.past_medical_history: Recurrent otitis media past 6 months, chronic sinusitis, no previous autoimmune disease
scenario.medications: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125mg BD (recently completed, PBS code: 1007B), ibuprofen 400mg PRN
scenario.social_history: Non-smoker, primary school teacher for 20 years, lives with husband and 2 teenage children, no pets
scenario.family_history: Mother has rheumatoid arthritis, no renal disease

physical_examination.general: Unwell appearance, saddle nose deformity developing, bilateral conjunctival injection
physical_examination.ent: Crusted bloody nasal discharge, septal perforation visible on examination, conductive hearing loss right ear
physical_examination.respiratory: Bilateral inspiratory crackles mid-zones, no wheeze, normal percussion
physical_examination.musculoskeletal: No active synovitis, no skin lesions
physical_examination.neurological: No focal deficits, no peripheral neuropathy

initial_tests.renal_function: Creatinine 156 μmol/L, urea 9.8 mmol/L, eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73m²
initial_tests.chest_xray: Multiple bilateral nodular opacities, largest 3cm right upper lobe with central cavitation

specialized_tests.anca: c-ANCA positive, PR3-ANCA strongly positive 158 U/mL (normal <20)
specialized_tests.hrct_chest: Multiple cavitating nodules, ground-glass opacities, tracheal wall thickening
specialized_tests.sinus_ct: Pansinusitis with bony erosion, nasal septal perforation
specialized_tests.tissue_biopsy: Transbronchial biopsy shows necrotising granulomatous inflammation with vasculitis

management_plan.induction_therapy: IV methylprednisolone 1g daily for 3 days then prednisolone 60mg daily (PBS code: 1950W), rituximab 375mg/m² weekly x 4 doses (PBS Authority code: 10329)
management_plan.maintenance: After remission: azathioprine 2mg/kg daily (PBS code: 2103D) with prednisolone taper over 6 months
management_plan.supportive: Cotrimoxazole 160/800mg daily for PCP prophylaxis (PBS code: 1649L), calcium 600mg + vitamin D 1000IU daily for bone protection
management_plan.monitoring: Monthly FBC, UEC, LFT during induction, regular PR3-ANCA levels, chest imaging every 3 months, audiometry for hearing

scoring_criteria: Recognises triad of upper respiratory, lower respiratory, and renal involvement (3 marks)
Orders c-ANCA/PR3 antibodies for diagnosis (3 marks)
Identifies saddle nose deformity as specific GPA feature (2 marks)
Arranges tissue biopsy for histological confirmation (2 marks)
Initiates induction therapy with rituximab or cyclophosphamide (3 marks)
Prescribes high-dose corticosteroids as bridging therapy (2 marks)
Includes PCP prophylaxis in treatment plan (2 marks)
Monitors for treatment-related infections and cytopenias (1 mark)
Arranges multidisciplinary care including ENT and nephrology (2 marks)
Discusses need for long-term maintenance therapy (1 mark)
Screens for subglottic stenosis as potential complication (1 mark)

title: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis - Whole Lung Lavage Indication

scenario.setting: Respiratory ward, St Vincent's Hospital, Sydney
scenario.presentation: A 38-year-old automotive spray painter presents with 6 months of progressive exertional dyspnoea and dry cough. He reports being unable to complete a full day's work due to breathlessness and has noticed his exercise tolerance declining from jogging 5km to barely managing one flight of stairs. No fever, no chest pain, no haemoptysis. He mentions his symptoms have gradually worsened despite two courses of antibiotics from his GP.

vital_signs.respiratory_rate: 20 breaths/min at rest, 32 with minimal exertion
vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: 89% on room air, 85% with exertion, 95% on 4L nasal prongs

scenario.past_medical_history: Nil significant, no previous respiratory disease
scenario.social_history: Automotive spray painter for 15 years with silica dust exposure, never smoker, drinks 2-3 beers weekly, lives with wife and 2 children
scenario.family_history: No lung disease, no autoimmune conditions

physical_examination.general: Well-nourished, mild respiratory distress with exertion, no clubbing, mild central cyanosis on exertion
physical_examination.cardiovascular: Normal heart sounds, no murmurs, no signs of pulmonary hypertension
physical_examination.respiratory: Fine inspiratory crackles bilaterally in mid and lower zones, no wheeze, normal percussion

initial_tests.arterial_blood_gas: pH 7.42, PaO2 62mmHg, PaCO2 35mmHg, HCO3 23mmol/L, A-a gradient 48mmHg
initial_tests.chest_xray: Bilateral perihilar alveolar opacities in 'bat-wing' distribution with relative sparing of apices and costophrenic angles

specialized_tests.hrct_chest: Bilateral ground-glass opacities with superimposed interlobular septal thickening ('crazy-paving' pattern), geographic distribution
specialized_tests.pulmonary_function_tests: FVC 68% predicted, FEV1 70% predicted, FEV1/FVC 85%, DLCO 42% predicted, severe reduction in DLCO
specialized_tests.bronchoscopy_bal: Milky, opaque fluid, PAS-positive proteinaceous material, foamy alveolar macrophages, no organisms on culture
specialized_tests.transbronchial_biopsy: Alveoli filled with PAS-positive granular eosinophilic material, preserved alveolar architecture

management_plan.definitive_treatment: Whole lung lavage under general anaesthesia, sequential lavage of each lung with 15-20L warm saline, 2-week interval between lungs
management_plan.pre_procedure: Optimise oxygenation, chest physiotherapy, ensure adequate nutrition (albumin >35g/L)
management_plan.alternative_therapy: If WLL contraindicated: subcutaneous GM-CSF 250μg daily for 12 weeks (specialist use only, not PBS listed)
management_plan.supportive: Supplemental oxygen PRN to maintain SpO2 >92%, pneumococcal and influenza vaccination, avoid further silica exposure
management_plan.monitoring: 6-monthly PFTs with DLCO, annual HRCT, monitor for superinfection

scoring_criteria: Identifies characteristic 'crazy-paving' pattern on HRCT (3 marks)
Recognises milky BAL fluid as pathognomonic finding (3 marks)
Orders anti-GM-CSF antibodies for autoimmune PAP diagnosis (2 marks)
Correctly interprets severely reduced DLCO with restrictive pattern (2 marks)
Recommends whole lung lavage as first-line treatment (3 marks)
Explains need for sequential bilateral lavage procedure (2 marks)
Identifies occupational silica exposure as secondary cause (2 marks)
Discusses GM-CSF therapy as alternative treatment option (1 mark)
Arranges appropriate pre-procedure optimisation (1 mark)
Plans long-term monitoring for disease recurrence (1 mark)
Counsels about infection risk and need for vaccinations (1 mark)

title: Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformation - Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia

scenario.setting: Respiratory consultation, Royal North Shore Hospital, Sydney
scenario.presentation: A 32-year-old accounts manager referred by her GP after an incidental finding on chest X-ray during a work health check. She reports occasional dyspnoea with exercise but attributed this to poor fitness. On direct questioning, she admits to frequent nosebleeds since childhood, averaging 3-4 per week, and her mother has similar issues. She had a small stroke 2 years ago with full recovery, cause never identified.
scenario.past_medical_history: Cryptogenic stroke age 30 with full recovery, iron deficiency anaemia, recurrent epistaxis
scenario.medications: Ferrous sulfate 325mg daily (PBS code: 2234Y), tranexamic acid 500mg PRN for nosebleeds
scenario.social_history: Non-smoker, office worker, married, trying to conceive, no illicit drugs
scenario.family_history: Mother has frequent nosebleeds and 'spots on her liver', maternal grandfather died of brain haemorrhage age 58

physical_examination.general: Well-appearing, mild central cyanosis, multiple small red spots on lips and tongue
physical_examination.skin: 2mm telangiectasias on lips, tongue, palmar surface of fingers, nasal mucosa
physical_examination.cardiovascular: Continuous machinery murmur left lower chest, normal heart sounds, no clubbing
physical_examination.respiratory: Clear lung fields, no crackles or wheeze
physical_examination.neurological: No focal deficits from previous stroke

initial_tests.chest_xray: 3cm rounded opacity left lower lobe with feeding artery and draining vein visible
initial_tests.arterial_blood_gas: pH 7.43, PaO2 68mmHg, PaCO2 32mmHg on room air, improves minimally with 100% O2 (shunt physiology)

specialized_tests.contrast_echocardiography: Positive bubble study with early left heart opacification within 3 cardiac cycles (grade 3 shunt)
specialized_tests.ct_pulmonary_angiography: Two PAVMs left lower lobe (3cm and 1.5cm), feeding artery 4mm diameter, multiple small PAVMs right lung
specialized_tests.cerebral_mri: Old right parietal infarct, no cerebral AVMs, no cavernomas
specialized_tests.abdominal_ultrasound: Multiple hepatic AVMs, no portal hypertension

differential_diagnosis: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia with pulmonary AVMs
Atrial septal defect with right-to-left shunt

management_plan.definitive_treatment: Urgent percutaneous transcatheter embolisation of PAVMs with feeding artery >3mm, use platinum coils or Amplatzer plugs
management_plan.pre_pregnancy: Must treat all treatable PAVMs before pregnancy due to increased rupture risk, genetic counselling (50% inheritance)
management_plan.antibiotic_prophylaxis: Prophylactic antibiotics for all dental/surgical procedures (risk of brain abscess), amoxicillin 2g PO 1 hour before
management_plan.long_term: Annual screening with contrast echo, MRI brain every 5 years for cerebral AVMs, avoid scuba diving permanently
management_plan.family_screening: Screen all first-degree relatives with contrast echocardiography and genetic testing

scoring_criteria: Recognises clinical triad of telangiectasias, recurrent epistaxis, and family history (3 marks)
Identifies orthodeoxia (desaturation on standing) as PAVM sign (2 marks)
Orders contrast echocardiography as screening test (2 marks)
Diagnoses hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia using Curacao criteria (2 marks)
Arranges urgent embolisation for PAVMs >3mm feeding artery (3 marks)
Recognises paradoxical embolism as stroke mechanism (2 marks)
Prescribes antibiotic prophylaxis for procedures (2 marks)
Screens for cerebral and hepatic AVMs (2 marks)
Provides pre-pregnancy counselling about risks (2 marks)
Arranges family screening and genetic counselling (2 marks)
